newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to build new prisons to ease overcrowding.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to build new prisons to ease overcrowding.

text.p: Brazil, troubled by a rash of violent rebellions in its overcrowded jails, will build 52 new small and medium-sized prisons by 1999, President Fernando Henrique Cardoso announced on Tuesday.

The new prisons would accommodate inmates currently packed into cells in police stations and jails in conditions "that mistreat people, provoke revolts and escapes and scare society as a whole," Cardoso said in a weekly radio address.

Prison riots have become an almost daily occurrence in Brazil and deaths are common. In Sao Paulo state alone, there have been about 60 rebellions so far this year. A 1995 census said 148,760 people were being held in Brazil's jails, which had only 76,000 places.
In his address, Cardoso said his government would spend nearly $300 million on the new prisons, which would offer inmates work on private-sector production lines within their walls.

He also said 60 projects to expand existing jails were under way and called on Congress to approve quickly a bill that would enable judges to sentence offenders to community service, or fine them, for crimes which currently carry jail terms.

"Countries like Germany, Britain and France adopted alternative sentencing more than 10 years ago and it is shown to recuperate prisoners and stop them from becoming more violent in day-to-day prison life," Cardoso said.
